quiz.title: CBSE Class 12 Maths 2006 Paper Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight board-level questions in the style of the 2006 paper, covering differentiation, integrals, matrices and determinants, vectors, 3D geometry and probability. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: If y = sin(x<sup>2</sup>), then dy/dx equals:
questions.explanation: By the chain rule, differentiate the outer sine to get cos(x<sup>2</sup>) and multiply by the derivative of the inner x<sup>2</sup>, which is 2x. So dy/dx = 2x cos(x<sup>2</sup>).

questions.q: If A is a 3 × 3 matrix with det(A) = 3, then det(adj A) equals:
questions.explanation: For an n × n matrix, det(adj A) = det(A)<sup>n−1</sup>. Here n = 3, so det(adj A) = 3<sup>2</sup> = 9.

questions.q: For vectors a and b with |a| = 2, |b| = 3 and the angle between them 30°, |a × b| equals:
If A and B are mutually exclusive events with P(A) = 0.5 and P(B) = 0.3, then P(A ∪ B) equals:
questions.explanation: For mutually exclusive events P(A ∩ B) = 0, so P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) = 0.5 + 0.3 = 0.8.

questions.q: The distance of the plane 2x − 2y + z = 6 from the origin is:
For any square matrix A, the matrix A + A<sup>T</sup> is always:
questions.explanation: (A + A<sup>T</sup>)<sup>T</sup> = A<sup>T</sup> + A = A + A<sup>T</sup>, so the matrix equals its own transpose and is therefore symmetric.

questions.q: ∫ from 0 to π of sin x dx equals:
questions.explanation: ∫ sin x dx = −cos x. Evaluating from 0 to π gives −cos π − (−cos 0) = −(−1) + 1 = 2.

faq.q: What topics does the CBSE Class 12 Mathematics 2006 paper cover?
faq.a: It follows the Class 12 syllabus of that year — differentiation and integration, matrices and determinants, vectors and three-dimensional geometry, differential equations, linear programming and probability. That spread is still the backbone of today's board paper.

faq.q: Is the 2006 paper still worth solving for the current CBSE exam?
faq.a: Yes. The methods it tests — chain-rule derivatives, standard integrals, determinant properties, dot and cross products — are unchanged. The pattern has since added objective and case-study sections, but the 2006 paper is clean drill for building core accuracy.

faq.q: How should I attempt a previous-year paper like this?
faq.a: Solve it in one timed sitting with no notes, then mark it honestly against the answer key and re-work only the questions you missed. That gap analysis fixes weak spots far faster than reading through solved answers.

faq.q: Which mistakes cost students the most marks on these questions?
faq.a: Forgetting the inner-derivative in chain-rule problems, sign slips during determinant expansion, and confusing the dot product (a scalar) with the cross product (a vector). Writing each step out prevents most of these.
